The appeal is filed challenging the order passed by the Tribunal in the judgment dated 31.03.2021 made in M.C.O.P.No.738 of 2010 on the file of Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, the Presiding Officer, Puducherry, dismissing the claimant's Claim Petition.

2. On 22.05.2009, while the appellant was riding pillion with her husband Babu in a motor cycle on Sedarapet Main Road, an oncoming motor cycle hit her husband's motor cycle, while he was trying to overtake an overloaded tractor trailer.
Due to the impact of the accident, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
According to the appellant, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the motor cycle and tractor trailer.
It was the appellant's contention that she was aged 21 years at the time of accident and was a house wife and after the accident, she could not do her work as before.
Therefore, the appellant filed the Claim Petition claiming a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- as compensation for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.
The 1st respondent, the owner of the motorcycle, which hit the motor cycle driven by the appellant's husband remained exparte before the Claims Tribunal.
The respondents 2 & 4, owners of the tractor and trailer respectively remained exparte before the Claims Tribunal.
The Claim Petition was contested by the respondents 3 & 5, the insurers of the tractor and trailer respectively.
The respondents 3 & 5 filed separate counters denying all the averments made in the Claim Petition apart from disputing the negligence, liability and quantum of compensation.
4. Before the Claims Tribunal, in support of her claim, the appellant examined herself as P.W.1 and Dr.Senthil was examined as P.W.2 and Exs.P1 to P19 were marked.
The 3rd respondent neither examined any witness nor marked any documents.
The 5 th respondent examined one Babu as R.W.1 and did not file any document.

The disability certificate was marked as Ex.C1.
5.
The Claims Tribunal, on an assessment of entire evidence on record, dismissed the Claim Petition.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
Aggrieved by the dismissal of the Claim Petition, the appellant has filed the present appeal challenging the finding of the Tribunal on negligence.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the trailer attached to the tractor was overloaded.
It was the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle that came in the opposite direction and the negligence of the driver of the tractor trailer, which resulted in the accident.
The counsel therefore submitted that the finding of Tribunal on negligence was unsustainable and it deserved to be set aside in the appeal.

8. Learned counsel for the respondents 3 & 5 on the other hand submitted that the Tribunal considering the facts and circumstances gave a reasoned finding and the same did not call for any interference in the appeal.
9. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondents 3 & 5 and perused the materials available on records.

sentences.text:
The appellant/claimant has averred in the Claim Petition as follows:
That on 22.5.2009 at about 15.15 hours when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider along with her husband, Mr.Babu in the Hero Honda motor cycle bearing Registration No.PY 01 AA 4055 after completing their program and was returning home along the Sedarapet Main Road and when they proceeded in front of Sree Tiles and Pavers, Sedarapet Main Road, Sedarapet, Pondicherry, the husband of the petitioner tried to overtake the Tractor bearing Registration No.PY 01 AT 8043 owned by the third respondent connecting a Trailer bearing Registration No.PY 01 D 0824 owned by the fifth respondent and a Tyre Cart containing heavy load of casuarian tree dried leaves with due caution and attentive and showing the sign of overtaking and at that time one Hero Honda Motor cycle CD 100 bearing Registration No.PY 01 4057 owned by the first respondent which was ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner hit against the petitioner's husband's motorcycle thereby both the petitioner and her husband were fallen on the road and the driver of the tractor who drove the tractor in a rash and negligent manner hit against the petitioner lying on https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the road thereby both the legs of the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, from the appellant's own pleadings, it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of the appellant's husband, who tried to overtake an overloaded tractor trailer.
Here again it is admitted by the appellant that her husband tried to overtake an overloaded tractor trailer.

12. In the light of the pleading as well as the evidence of appellant, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis it is clear that the husband of the claimant was negligent in trying to overtake the overloaded tractor trailer.
As the tractor trailer was overloaded, the husband of the appellant could not have seen the oncoming motor cycle.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly held that the negligence of the appellant's husband resulted in the accident.
I find absolutely no infirmity in the order of the Tribunal and therefore, the finding of the Tribunal on negligence is confirmed.
In my view, there are no merits in the appeal and therefore, the same is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
